## **Mastering Your Clinical Interview: Expert Insights from HCSG Recruiters**


[Careers](https://www.hcsgcorp.com/blog/category/careers/) ,


[Nutrition](https://www.hcsgcorp.com/blog/category/nutrition/)


Job interviews can feel intimidating, but they are also your best opportunity to discover more about the role, connect with potential coworkers, and demonstrate how your clinical expertise drives meaningful outcomes. Discover the key recommendations Healthcare Services Group (HCSG) Clinical Recruiters Kate Boyle and Natalie Shires share to help you prepare effectively and step into your interview with total confidence.


****Get to Know Our Company****


Researching our organization prior to your interview provides essential context about our operational scope and culture. As the largest employer of registered dietitians in the industry,[HCSG offers extensive opportunities](http://rd.careers/) for career advancement, access to a broad clinical community, and the chance to make a direct, meaningful impact on resident care.


****Prepare Questions****


An interview is a two-way street. Coming prepared with thoughtful, specific questions demonstrates your initiative, critical thinking, and genuine interest in the position. Tailor your questions to cover company growth, team culture, and daily clinical expectations to help determine if the role aligns with your career goals.


***Insightful Questions to Ask Your Interviewer:***


- *What structure and mentorship are provided during the orientation and training period for a new Registered Dietitian?*
- *How does HCSG support ongoing clinical education, professional development, and career advancement?*
- *What key milestones or outcomes define a successful first 90 days in this role?*
- *How do dietitians on this team collaborate with multidisciplinary care staff and facility leadership?*


****Be Engaged****


Staying engaged and showing genuine excitement during your interview can leave a strong, positive impression. Take a moment to relax so your enthusiasm comes through naturally. Pay attention to non-verbal cues: sit up straight, maintain good posture, make appropriate eye contact, and smile to convey confidence.


On virtual calls, look directly at the camera when speaking to simulate eye contact. Keep movements natural—avoid fidgeting or adjusting your device, and offer a confident handshake in person when appropriate.


****Showcase Your Experience & Clinical Impact****


Don’t just describe your responsibilities—share specific examples of how you made a difference for patients, residents, or clients. Highlight nutrition interventions, improved outcomes, problem-solving, and other accomplishments.


New graduate? Your clinical rotations count! Use your rotations, internships, coursework, and projects to demonstrate your clinical knowledge and communication skills. Be ready to share a patient or resident example and explain the concern, your assessment, intervention, and outcome.


***💡 Use the STAR method to organize your answers and demonstrate problem-solving skills.***


****Follow Up & Send a Thank-You Note****


Always follow up with your recruiter or hiring manager within 24 hours of your interview. Express sincere gratitude for their time, reiterate your enthusiasm for the position, and briefly highlight how your specific clinical skills and values align with the role. A prompt, personalized thank-you email reinforces your professionalism, keeps you top of mind, and leaves a strong final impression.


****Additional Tips****


- **Use Your Online Network** – keep your LinkedIn profile up to date and get connected with your peers. You never know who can open the door to your next opportunity!
- **Practice Interviewing** – Interviews can bring up a range of emotions. Find a peer, friend, or family member to conduct a ‘mock interview’ with you to ease the jitters and practice your responses to common interview questions.
- **Dress for Success** – Choose professional attire appropriate for a healthcare environment so you feel confident and comfortable.
- **Be On Time** – Whether you are traveling to an interview location or hopping onto a video call, arrive a few minutes early to give yourself time to relax, get composed, and be mentally prepared to ace your interview.


An interview is your opportunity to present your authentic self, communicate your value effectively, and showcase the tangible impact you bring to patient and resident care. By leveraging these strategies, you can navigate your interview with confidence and take a decisive step forward in your clinical career.
